shape_construction: Believable task-specific proportions, silhouettes, construction, joins and object anatomy. Generic boxes, disconnected pipes, floating parts and unclosed architectural gaps are substantive defects. Judge intended stylization, not polygon count.
materials: Appropriate authored material vocabulary, scale, surface differentiation and consistency. Default/checker surfaces, indiscriminate tiling and texture pasted over primitive geometry do not establish finish. Do not demand wear where not requested.
lighting: Exposure, readable surfaces, shadow depth, light/material relationships across all important zones. Burnt-out whites, persistent darkness, flat unreadable surfaces and pervasive glare lower quality even if objects exist.
composition: Spatial hierarchy, focal readability, coherent massing and purposeful distribution at overview, street/room and close scales. Empty space is not inherently bad; unjustified barren requested working or inhabited zones are.
detail: Meaningful task-specific equipment, furnishing and environmental detail at large/medium/small scales. Repeated colored boxes, labels and token props cannot stand in for differentiated functional objects or rich requested spaces.
style: Match the requested/reference visual language across all zones. Real environments require plausible construction and material treatment; voxel/game styles require intentional resolved abstraction. Do not penalize coherent low-poly/voxel design for not being photorealistic.
scene_coverage: Substantive realization of the public brief and reference scene extent, connected zones, context and principal architectural/environmental features. Judge the realized scene, not merely presence counts or labels. Avoid requiring identical camera or incidental photograph clutter.
functional_identity: Visible differentiation and credible furnishing of required functional areas and mechanisms. A named room with token objects is partial credit. Compare defining reference features when supplied. Do not infer actual interactive success from appearance.

formula: continuous quality anchored to visible completion; coverage and deviation retained separately as diagnostics

environment.criterion: Arrange the forecourt, successive gates and principal hall courtyard along a coherent central processional axis, preserving the frontal symmetry of the reference views.
Maintain monumental proportions: tall defensive walls, deep gate openings, expansive courts and a broad stair ascent beneath the dominant palace hall.
Keep courtyard centers broad and predominantly paved, with ornament concentrated along approach edges and stair landings; preserve the sparse visible vegetation.
Match clear blue sky, strong daylight and directional shadows, with weathered ochre masonry, muted gray paving and roofs, and restrained red timber accents.

features.criterion: A broad crenellated wall centers on one tall rectangular entrance, flanked by two enormous symmetrical horned mask reliefs.
A red colonnaded pavilion with two stacked tiled roof levels rises above the wall, with smaller elevated towers at both sides.
The entrance has a thick dark ornamental surround, red inner jambs and a rectangular framed plaque above.
Rough ochre stone contrasts with charcoal reliefs, faded red structural members and gray roof tiles.

targets.label: Outer forecourt gate and mask wall

features.criterion: A massive crenellated wall contains three openings, with the central passage taller and wider than the flanking passages.
Each passage has angular clipped upper corners and a heavy dark frame surrounding a visibly deep interior.
A central pavilion has three progressively smaller roof tiers, broad upturned eaves and a short projecting balustraded balcony.
Weathered yellow-gray wall surfaces surround dark timber pavilion bays and closely ribbed gray tiled roofs.
The principal hall presents a very wide symmetrical facade beneath three long stacked roof tiers with gently rising corners.
A monumental central stone staircase spans much of the hall frontage, accompanied by narrower lateral stair flights.
Repeated red columns and projecting brackets support the deep front eaves above recessed dark door bays.
Pale balustrades border terraces and stairs, contrasting with dark gray steps, gray tiles, ochre wall panels and red timber.

targets.label: Principal palace hall and stair terraces

features.criterion: Lower galleries frame the main approaches, while taller square towers punctuate the gate flanks.
Gallery roofs form long low tiled runs with projecting eaves; tower roofs cap stacked open balcony levels.
Gray roof tiles, muted red posts, pale railings and warm plaster panels repeat the principal buildings' palette.
Expansive level courts create long unobstructed approaches to the centered gateways and staircase.
Rectangular paving modules form regular axial rows with repeated shallow geometric surface patterns.
Raised curbs and narrow pale gravel strips border the inner gate approach; linear edge channels remain subordinate to the paving.
Paving has a worn gray-beige stone appearance with visible joints and subtle tonal variation.
Paired dark sculptural beasts or birds stand on plinths beside gateways and stair approaches.
The hall staircase is accented by guardian figures on tall square pedestals bearing large carved relief panels.
Tall crossbar standards carry narrow purple banners near the inner gate, while elongated red lantern standards line the hall approach.
Dark weathered sculptural surfaces and carved stone bases contrast with red and purple hanging fabric.
